clue.text: The party chief's field of knowledge

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or social event
main as an adjective means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A political party leader's area of expertise is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party chief' reads as a political leader, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a sphere of learning or activity that someone has mastered, a subject area.

clue.text: Warmth mainly in the centre of power

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so only most of the phrase's word is used, its tail dropped

parts.note: AMID means in the centre of; only most of it is kept
ability is the power to do something

explanation.surface: Someone is asking for warmth to sit chiefly at the heart of authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' means most of: AMID loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiability is friendliness and good nature, the personal warmth of an agreeable person.

clue.text: Points once made by Wilson

parts.note: surface reading: arguments a politician called Wilson once put forward, perhaps Harold Wilson
setter's reading: the number of points in US President Woodrow Wilson's famous 1918 peace programme

explanation.surface: A historical note on arguments once advanced by a politician named Wilson.
explanation.walkthrough: British solvers think first of Harold Wilson; it is Woodrow Wilson, whose 1918 plan for peace after the First World War was known by the number of its points.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points set out his proposed terms for ending the First World War.

clue.text: Right page and right for the churchman

parts.note: the recto is the right-hand page of an open book
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Instructions for laying out a correct page for a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a member of the clergy in charge of a parish, so a churchman.

clue.text: Tries in a short dance to prepare for performance

indicators.note: a short version of a word is one cut off before its final letter
one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance; cut short it loses its last letter
a judge hears or tries a case in court

explanation.surface: Someone attempts a brief dance routine before going on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like attempts, but it is the courtroom sense: a judge tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a play, piece or routine in readiness for the real show.

clue.text: Note short time taken in decorative work

indicators.note: something taken in is absorbed or enclosed by what surrounds it

parts.note: crochet is decorative needlework made with a hooked needle
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A brief message about how little time went into some ornamental handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is a musical note, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note lasting one beat, called a quarter note in American usage.

clue.text: Polish? That's what I am!

parts.note: to polish something is to make it smooth
i.e. abbreviates the Latin id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A boastful speaker claims to be the very embodiment of polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' at the start of the clue hides its lower-case sense behind the capital: it is shine, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is a suave, polished person, which is what the self-satisfied speaker claims to be.

clue.text: Obscure old land measure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to conceal or keep out of sight
second meaning: an old English unit of land, enough to support a family

explanation.surface: A little-known historical unit for measuring fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' reads as an adjective qualifying the measure, but it is a verb in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide is to conceal; a hide was also an Anglo-Saxon area of farmland, around 120 acres.

clue.text: Currency? Ex officio, the City is included

indicators.note: something included is held within a larger whole, so it goes inside

parts.note: EO is the abbreviation of ex officio, by virtue of office
Ur was the ancient Sumerian city, a favourite crossword city

explanation.surface: A question of whether City finance officials sit on a monetary committee by right of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The City' suggests the City of London's financial district, which suits currency, but it is the ancient city of Ur.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the common money used by most member states of the European Union.

clue.text: Water pipe

parts.note: surface reading: a plumbing conduit carrying water
setter's reading: a smoking pipe in which the smoke is drawn through water

explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound like plumbing; the pipe is for smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: A hookah is an oriental tobacco pipe whose smoke is cooled by passing through a water vessel.

clue.text: Most of barrow lad upset — in a pet, possibly?

indicators.note: most of a word is all but a bit of it, here the last letter
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a barrow is a cart; most of the word is kept, dropping its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy with a wheelbarrow is in a sulk, in a pet as the British say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a pet' looks like the idiom for being in a huff; here 'a pet, possibly' defines, since a dog is one kind of pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labrador is a breed of dog, commonly kept as a family companion, so an example of a pet.

clue.text: Recount aria performed anew — an expression of denial?

indicators.note: performing something anew means doing it over in a fresh version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words are used

explanation.surface: An opera singer is told to go over the aria again and sing it afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Au contraire is French for 'on the contrary', a phrase used to contradict what has just been said.

clue.text: King in aggro to become settled. Ready for it?

indicators.note: things that become settled are put in a new order after disturbance, so the letters rearrange

parts.note: R abbreviates rex, Latin for king
the letters are used as written

explanation.surface: A furious monarch is urged to calm down, and asked if he is prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone raring to go is eager and impatient to start, fully ready for the task ahead.

clue.text: Skilfully holds breach when river goes unexpectedly

indicators.note: the river's name departing means those letters are struck from the word
a word that holds another wraps around it and keeps it inside

parts.note: ably means skilfully
a breach is a rupture; the Ure, a Yorkshire river, is removed from its end

explanation.surface: A dam cleverly contains a breach when the river suddenly bursts through.
explanation.definitionFit: Abruptly means suddenly and without warning, so happening in an unforeseen way.

clue.text: Animal to control rising grass

parts.note: to rein is to control, as a rider checks a horse

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upward, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands

explanation.surface: A grazing creature needs restraining as the grass grows up.
explanation.definitionFit: A reindeer is an Arctic member of the deer family, used for herding and pulling sleds.

clue.text: One mailing letters about pound being inadequate

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: one who posts letters is their sender
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone posting letters complains that a pound does not cover the postage.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slight or meagre, as in slender means or a slender chance, so not enough.

clue.text: Dismantle wreck

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pull down a building or structure
second meaning: to ruin or destroy utterly, as an argument

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as an instruction to take apart a wrecked vehicle; each is a verb meaning the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To demolish is to knock down a structure and, figuratively, to destroy something completely.

clue.text: Trouble in globe is common

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so its letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters are used as written

explanation.surface: A world-weary remark that strife around the world is widespread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' is not frequent but low-born, its old social sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble originally meant of humble birth, not of the nobility, which is the snobbish sense of common.

clue.text: Means of lighting possessed by the super-rich?

definitions.text: Means of lighting possessed by the super-rich

parts.note: surface reading: lamps or fuel that the wealthy own
setter's reading: wealth so plentiful it could be set alight, means being money

explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like a method, but it is the financial sense, a person's resources; the idiom pictures them as fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Having more cash than one needs is described by an idiom imagining surplus banknotes used as kindling.

clue.text: Expert for boat without a bow

indicators.note: a vessel's bow is its front, so lacking it means losing the opening letter

parts.note: a coracle is a small round wicker boat; its first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A specialist is sought for a vessel that is missing its front end.
explanation.walkthrough: A bow is the front of a boat, so the word loses its front letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person regarded as an infallible authority, someone whose advice is sought.

clue.text: People first do the repair

parts.note: men are people

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: An instruction for people to carry out a fix before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something is to fix it, the verb sense of repair, putting broken things right.

clue.text: An area of sacred ground

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the answer is a portion of the following letters

parts.note: found inside the first of these words

explanation.surface: A plot of holy land, such as a churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' marks letters taken out of the next word; 'God's acre' is an old name for a churchyard, which makes the surface fit.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, about 4,047 square metres.

clue.text: Develop opera house in summer in Europe

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: ete is French for summer
La Scala in Milan is the world's best-known opera house

explanation.surface: Plans to build an opera house during a European summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Europe' tells you to use another European language for summer: French.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to grow or intensify, as a situation develops into something larger.

clue.text: Keep the piece

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fortified tower of a stronghold
second meaning: a chess piece, also called a rook

explanation.surface: Someone is told to retain the item rather than give it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb meaning retain; it is the noun for a stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a fortified building whose innermost tower is the keep, and it also names the rook in chess.

clue.text: Horse training to dip in tangled reeds

indicators.note: a word placed in another goes inside it
something tangled is twisted out of its order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
to sag is to dip or droop

explanation.surface: A rider's horse must learn to plunge through a mass of tangled waterside plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the art of schooling a horse in precise, controlled movements, judged in competition.

clue.text: Musician in quiet band

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a layer is a band or stratum of material

explanation.surface: A performer belongs to a softly playing group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a musical group, which suits the surface, but it is a stripe or stratum.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who plays an instrument, a performer of music.
